- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 5–10% in subsequent periods.  
- When true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to correct — apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 3-day average + 10% of recent drop.  
- If history shows consistent downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive declines), model often underestimates further drop — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overreact to minor price moves — dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in early horizon.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early period (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history includes 0.5+ for 2+ consecutive days, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
